ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT
(Tracked-Changes Redline — Counsel Markup of Counterparty Draft)
================================================================================
DOCUMENT STATUS: Working redline for negotiation
PREPARED FOR: Secured Party / Lender counsel review
SOURCE PAPER: Counterparty (Depository Bank) draft Account Control Agreement
REFERENCE SET: Internal ACA Playbook; Executed Credit Agreement; Bank standard form;
               Account schedule / account details; closing checklist & correspondence
MARKUP KEY:
  [DELETE: …] = text to be deleted from counterparty draft
  [INSERT: …] = text to be inserted
  [MOVE: …]   = relocation
  **COMMENT** = negotiation note (not operative)
================================================================================

ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT

This ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”), dated as of [________], 20[__] (the “Effective Date”), is entered into by and among:

(i)  [BORROWER LEGAL NAME], a [jurisdiction] [entity type] (the “Debtor”);
(ii) [ADMINISTRATIVE AGENT / COLLATERAL AGENT LEGAL NAME], as [administrative agent / collateral agent] for the Secured Parties under the Credit Agreement referred to below (in such capacity, together with its successors and assigns in such capacity, the “Secured Party”); and
(iii) [DEPOSITORY BANK LEGAL NAME] (the “Bank”).

The Debtor, the Secured Party and the Bank are referred to herein collectively as the “Parties” and individually as a “Party.”

RECITALS

A.  The Debtor and certain of its affiliates, the lenders party thereto from time to time, and the Secured Party have entered into that certain [Credit Agreement], dated as of [________], 20[__] (as amended, restated, supplemented, refinanced, replaced or otherwise modified from time to time, the “Credit Agreement”), pursuant to which the lenders have agreed to extend credit to the Debtor and its affiliates on the terms and conditions set forth therein.

B.  Pursuant to the Credit Agreement and that certain [Security / Pledge / Collateral Agreement], dated as of [________], 20[__] (as amended, restated, supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time, the “Security Agreement”), the Debtor has granted to the Secured Party, for the benefit of the Secured Parties, a security interest in, among other things, the Account (as defined below) and all cash, funds, financial assets, securities entitlements, instruments, investment property and other property credited thereto or carried therein from time to time (collectively, the “Collateral”).

C.  The Debtor maintains with the Bank the deposit account[s] identified on Schedule I hereto (as the same may be amended, supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time in accordance with this Agreement, each an “Account” and collectively the “Accounts”).

D.  The Parties are entering into this Agreement to perfect the Secured Party’s security interest in the Accounts and the Collateral by “control” within the meaning of Sections 9-104 and, to the extent applicable, 8-106 and 9-106 of the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in the State of New York (the “UCC”), and to set forth the Bank’s agreement to comply with instructions originated by the Secured Party directing disposition of the funds in the Accounts without further consent by the Debtor.

AGREEMENT

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements herein contained, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 1.  DEFINITIONS; INTERPRETATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.1  Definitions.  Capitalized terms used but not defined herein have the meanings ascribed to them in the Credit Agreement or the Security Agreement, as applicable.  In addition, as used herein:

“Business Day” means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or other day on which commercial banks in New York, New York [INSERT: or in the city in which the office of the Bank at which the Accounts are maintained is located] are authorized or required by law to close.

“Control Notice” [DELETE: means a written notice from the Secured Party to the Bank substantially in the form of Exhibit A stating that the Secured Party is exercising exclusive control over the Accounts.] [INSERT: means a written notice from the Secured Party to the Bank, substantially in the form of Exhibit A (or in such other form as the Secured Party may determine in its reasonable discretion), stating that the Secured Party is exercising its right to exclusive control over the Accounts and directing the Bank thereafter to comply solely with instructions originated by the Secured Party with respect to the Accounts and the Collateral, without further consent by the Debtor.]

“Excluded Claims” has the meaning set forth in Section 5.2.

“Indemnified Persons” has the meaning set forth in Section 8.1.

“Instructions” means instructions originated by the Secured Party directing the disposition of funds from time to time in the Accounts, including without limitation any Control Notice and any other entitlement orders, payment orders, fund transfer instructions or other directions with respect to the Accounts or the Collateral.

“Obligations” means all obligations, liabilities and indebtedness of every kind of the Debtor and the other Loan Parties to the Secured Party and the other Secured Parties under or in connection with the Credit Agreement, the Security Agreement, the other Loan Documents and this Agreement, whether now existing or hereafter arising, direct or indirect, absolute or contingent, due or to become due.

“Secured Parties” has the meaning ascribed to such term in the Credit Agreement.

“UCC” means the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect from time to time in the State of New York; provided that, if by reason of mandatory provisions of law, perfection, the effect of perfection or non-perfection, or the priority of any security interest is governed by the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in a jurisdiction other than the State of New York, “UCC” means the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in such other jurisdiction for purposes of the provisions hereof relating to such perfection, effect of perfection or non-perfection or priority.

1.2  UCC Terms.  Terms defined in Articles 8 or 9 of the UCC and not otherwise defined herein have the meanings ascribed to them therein (including, without limitation, “control,” “deposit account,” “entitlement order,” “financial asset,” “investment property,” “proceeds” and “securities entitlement”).

1.3  Rules of Construction.  The rules of construction set forth in the Credit Agreement apply mutatis mutandis to this Agreement.  References to “including” mean “including without limitation.”  Section headings are for convenience only and shall not affect interpretation.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 2.  THE ACCOUNTS; ESTABLISHMENT OF CONTROL
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

2.1  Identification of Accounts.  The Bank confirms that (a) the Debtor is the Bank’s customer with respect to each Account, (b) each Account is a “deposit account” as defined in Section 9-102(a) of the UCC, (c) the account number, title and other identifying information for each Account are correctly set forth on Schedule I, and (d) [DELETE: to the Bank’s knowledge,] the Bank has not entered into any currently effective agreement with any person other than the Secured Party by which the Bank has agreed to comply with instructions originated by such person directing disposition of the funds in any Account without further consent by the Debtor.  [INSERT: The Bank represents and warrants that Schedule I is complete and accurate as of the Effective Date and agrees to update Schedule I promptly upon the opening of any additional account that is required to be subject to this Agreement pursuant to the Credit Agreement or the Security Agreement.]

2.2  Subordination of Liens; Waiver of Set-Off.
(a)  The Bank hereby subordinates any security interest, lien, encumbrance, claim, right of set-off, right of recoupment, bankers’ lien or other right that the Bank may have in or against any Account or any Collateral (other than Excluded Claims) to the security interest of the Secured Party in the Accounts and the Collateral.
(b)  [DELETE: Except as provided in Section 5, the Bank agrees that it will not exercise any right of set-off, banker’s lien or other claim against any Account.] [INSERT: The Bank agrees that it shall not exercise or claim any security interest, lien, right of set-off, right of recoupment, bankers’ lien or other right in or against any Account or any Collateral, other than Excluded Claims expressly permitted under Section 5.2, and any such exercise or claim (other than with respect to Excluded Claims) shall be void as against the Secured Party.]
(c)  [INSERT: The Bank’s subordination and waiver under this Section 2.2 is automatic and continuing and shall remain effective until the Secured Party has delivered a written termination notice in accordance with Section 10.]

2.3  Control.  The Bank agrees that it will comply with Instructions originated by the Secured Party directing disposition of the funds in the Accounts [DELETE: after receipt of a Control Notice and] without further consent by the Debtor.  [INSERT: The Parties acknowledge and agree that the Secured Party has “control” (within the meaning of Section 9-104(a)(2) of the UCC) of each Account on and after the Effective Date, and that such control is established by this Agreement itself and does not require delivery of a Control Notice as a condition to perfection.  Delivery of a Control Notice shall solely effect a change in the operational disposition regime from “Debtor direction permitted until notice” to “exclusive Secured Party direction,” as set forth in Section 3.]  The Bank shall have no duty to inquire into the authority of the person giving any Instruction on behalf of the Secured Party or the appropriateness of any Instruction, and shall be fully protected in acting on any Instruction that the Bank reasonably believes to have been given by an authorized representative of the Secured Party.

2.4  [INSERT: No Other Control Agreements.  The Bank shall not enter into any other control agreement, blocked account agreement or similar arrangement with respect to any Account in favor of any person other than the Secured Party without the prior written consent of the Secured Party.]

2.5  [INSERT: Additional Accounts.  If the Debtor opens any additional deposit account with the Bank that is required under the Credit Agreement or the Security Agreement to be subject to a control agreement in favor of the Secured Party, the Debtor and the Bank shall promptly (and in any event within five (5) Business Days) execute and deliver a supplement to Schedule I (or an amendment or joinder to this Agreement in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to the Secured Party) bringing such account within the scope of this Agreement, and such account shall thereafter constitute an “Account” for all purposes hereof.]

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 3.  OPERATION OF THE ACCOUNTS; CONTROL NOTICE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

3.1  Pre-Control Notice Operation.  Until the Bank receives a Control Notice from the Secured Party:
(a)  the Bank may [DELETE: shall] comply with instructions originated by the Debtor directing disposition of the funds in the Accounts [INSERT: , unless such instructions conflict with any standing Instruction from the Secured Party then in effect];
(b)  the Debtor may make withdrawals, transfers and other dispositions from the Accounts in the ordinary course; and
(c)  [INSERT: nothing in this Section 3.1 shall impair or limit the Secured Party’s perfected security interest in, or control over, the Accounts and the Collateral, which shall remain continuously perfected by control from and after the Effective Date.]

3.2  Control Notice; Exclusive Control.
(a)  The Secured Party may deliver a Control Notice to the Bank at any time in the Secured Party’s sole discretion [DELETE: following the occurrence of an Event of Default under the Credit Agreement].  [INSERT: **COMMENT: Playbook and Credit Agreement require unfettered right to deliver Control Notice at any time; linkage to Event of Default is off-market and unacceptable for perfection/enforcement timing.**]
(b)  Upon the Bank’s receipt of a Control Notice (and at all times thereafter until this Agreement is terminated in accordance with Section 10):
    (i)   the Bank shall cease complying with instructions originated by the Debtor with respect to the Accounts;
    (ii)  the Bank shall comply solely with Instructions originated by the Secured Party directing disposition of funds in the Accounts, without further consent by the Debtor;
    (iii) the Debtor shall have no further right to withdraw, transfer or otherwise dispose of any funds or other Collateral in the Accounts, except as expressly directed or consented to in writing by the Secured Party; and
    (iv)  [INSERT: the Bank shall, within one (1) Business Day of receipt of the Control Notice, confirm in writing to the Secured Party (with a copy to the Debtor) that the Control Notice has been received and implemented.]
(c)  [INSERT: The Bank’s obligation to comply with the Secured Party’s Instructions after receipt of a Control Notice is absolute and unconditional and is not subject to any condition precedent (including any requirement that the Secured Party certify as to the existence of a default or Event of Default), any cure or notice period, or any inquiry into the merits of the Instruction.]

3.3  Form and Delivery of Instructions.  Instructions (including any Control Notice) shall be in writing and delivered in accordance with Section 11.  [INSERT: Instructions transmitted by email PDF or other electronic transmission from an email address of a person designated by the Secured Party on Schedule II (as updated from time to time by the Secured Party) shall be deemed duly given writing.]  The Bank may rely on any Instruction that it reasonably believes to be genuine and to have been signed or sent by an authorized person, and shall have no duty to verify authenticity beyond confirming that the Instruction purports to be from the Secured Party [INSERT: consistent with the authorized persons list on Schedule II then in effect].

3.4  [DELETE: The Bank shall have a reasonable period of time, not to exceed three (3) Business Days, to implement any Control Notice or other Instruction.] [INSERT: The Bank shall implement any Control Notice as promptly as practicable and in any event no later than the close of business on the Business Day of receipt if received before 12:00 noon (local time at the Bank’s office), or otherwise by the close of business on the next Business Day.  Other Instructions shall be implemented within one (1) Business Day of receipt (or such shorter period as is operationally feasible for wire and ACH cut-offs).]

3.5  [INSERT: Standing Disposition Instructions.  Prior to delivery of a Control Notice, the Secured Party may from time to time deliver standing Instructions regarding minimum balances, sweeps to a concentration account designated by the Secured Party, or other disposition mechanics, and the Bank shall implement such standing Instructions upon written confirmation by the Debtor (which confirmation the Debtor hereby agrees to provide promptly upon request by the Secured Party consistent with the Credit Agreement).  After a Control Notice, no Debtor confirmation shall be required.]

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 4.  BANK’S RESPONSIBILITIES AND STANDARD OF CARE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

4.1  Duties Limited.  The Bank undertakes to perform only such duties as are expressly set forth herein.  [DELETE: The Bank shall not be liable for any action taken or omitted except in the case of its gross negligence or willful misconduct.] [INSERT: The Bank shall exercise the same care in performing its duties under this Agreement as it exercises with respect to similar accounts maintained for its other account holders, and the Bank shall be liable for its negligence, willful misconduct or bad faith (as finally determined by a court of competent jurisdiction).  **COMMENT: “Gross negligence only” is off-market for bank operational failures on control accounts; playbook requires ordinary negligence standard.**]

4.2  No Implied Duties; No Monitoring.  The Bank shall have no duty to (a) monitor the Debtor’s compliance with the Credit Agreement or any other Loan Document, (b) determine whether an Event of Default exists, (c) review the contents of any Instruction other than to confirm it is given by the Secured Party, or (d) take any action not expressly required hereunder.  [INSERT: Nothing in this Section 4.2 shall relieve the Bank of its express obligations under Sections 2, 3, 5 and 6.]

4.3  Permitted Reliance.  The Bank may rely upon, and shall not be liable for action taken or omitted in reliance upon, any Instruction, notice, or other document reasonably believed by it to be genuine and to have been signed or presented by the proper Party.

4.4  [INSERT: Force Majeure.  The Bank shall not be liable for any failure or delay in performance due to circumstances beyond its reasonable control (including acts of God, war, terrorism, civil unrest, embargo, fire, flood, pandemic, or failure of utilities or communications systems not caused by the Bank); provided that the Bank shall (i) give prompt notice to the Secured Party and the Debtor and (ii) use commercially reasonable efforts to resume performance as soon as practicable.  Force majeure shall not excuse the Bank’s failure to maintain the subordination and control arrangements under Sections 2 and 3 once systems are restored.]

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 5.  BANK FEES; EXCLUDED CLAIMS; STATEMENTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

5.1  Fees and Expenses.  The Debtor agrees to pay the Bank’s fees and charges for the Accounts and for the Bank’s services under this Agreement in accordance with the Bank’s standard fee schedule [INSERT: as disclosed to the Debtor and the Secured Party prior to the Effective Date, or as otherwise agreed in a written fee letter among the Parties], as in effect from time to time.  [DELETE: The Bank may debit the Accounts for such fees and charges at any time.] [INSERT: The Bank may debit the Accounts for such fees and charges only to the extent constituting Excluded Claims under Section 5.2, and only so long as no Control Notice is in effect or, if a Control Notice is in effect, only with the prior written consent of the Secured Party or pursuant to a court order.  The Debtor remains primarily liable for all such fees.]

5.2  Excluded Claims.  Notwithstanding Section 2.2, the Bank may exercise rights of set-off and charge-back against the Accounts solely with respect to the following (collectively, “Excluded Claims”), and only to the extent arising in respect of the Accounts:
(a)  the Bank’s customary fees and charges for maintenance and operation of the Accounts [INSERT: to the extent not past due more than thirty (30) days];
(b)  returned items, reversals, chargebacks, corrections and adjustments with respect to items deposited to or paid from the Accounts, [INSERT: limited to items deposited or initiated not more than one hundred eighty (180) days prior to the exercise of such right]; and
(c)  [DELETE: any other obligations of the Debtor to the Bank, whether or not related to the Accounts.] [INSERT: overdrafts on the Accounts and returned deposited items, in each case solely with respect to the Account against which the overdraft or returned item arose.  **COMMENT: Open-ended “any other obligations” set-off is a critical playbook red flag and must be deleted; Excluded Claims must be account-specific and cabined.**]

[INSERT: 5.2A  Priority of Excluded Claims.  The Bank’s rights in respect of Excluded Claims shall be senior to the Secured Party’s security interest only to the extent of unpaid Excluded Claims actually arising, and the aggregate amount of Excluded Claims asserted against the Accounts at any time after delivery of a Control Notice shall not exceed $[______] without the Secured Party’s prior written consent (the “Excluded Claims Cap”).]

5.3  Account Statements; Information Access.
(a)  The Bank shall provide to the Secured Party [DELETE: upon request] [INSERT: automatically, concurrently with delivery to the Debtor (and in any event not less frequently than monthly),] copies of all account statements, notices of returned items, and other account-level notices with respect to the Accounts that the Bank provides to the Debtor.
(b)  [INSERT: The Bank shall, upon reasonable request of the Secured Party, provide balance and transaction information with respect to the Accounts (including via online access on a view-only basis if available) and confirm in writing the account balances as of a specified date and time.]
(c)  [INSERT: The Debtor hereby authorizes and directs the Bank to provide all such information and access to the Secured Party without further consent or inquiry.]

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 6.  REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

6.1  Bank Representations.  The Bank represents and warrants to the Secured Party as of the Effective Date [INSERT: and on each date on which an additional Account is added to Schedule I] that:
(a)  it is a [bank / national banking association / state-chartered bank] duly organized, validly existing and in good standing under the laws of its jurisdiction of organization, and has all requisite power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement;
(b)  this Agreement has been duly authorized, executed and delivered by the Bank and constitutes the legal, valid and binding obligation of the Bank, enforceable against the Bank in accordance with its terms, except as enforceability may be limited by bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium or similar laws affecting creditors’ rights generally and by general principles of equity;
(c)  the execution, delivery and performance of this Agreement do not conflict with or result in a breach of the Bank’s organizational documents or any material agreement binding upon the Bank or any law or regulation applicable to the Bank in any material respect;
(d)  each Account is maintained in the ordinary course of the Bank’s business, is a “deposit account” under Section 9-102(a) of the UCC, and the Debtor is the Bank’s sole customer with respect to each Account [INSERT: except for any joint account structure expressly identified on Schedule I and consented to by the Secured Party];
(e)  the Bank has not entered into any currently effective agreement with any third party agreeing to comply with instructions originated by such third party directing disposition of funds in any Account without further consent of the Debtor; and
(f)  [INSERT: the Bank has not received notice of any adverse claim to any Account or any funds therein, other than the security interest of the Secured Party contemplated hereby.]

6.2  Debtor Representations.  The Debtor represents and warrants to the Secured Party and the Bank that:
(a)  it is the sole owner of each Account and the sole entitlement holder / customer with respect thereto;
(b)  it has not granted any security interest in any Account or the Collateral (other than the security interest in favor of the Secured Party and other Permitted Liens under the Credit Agreement, if any, that are junior and expressly permitted);
(c)  the execution, delivery and performance of this Agreement have been duly authorized and this Agreement constitutes its legal, valid and binding obligation; and
(d)  [INSERT: each Account is a Collateral Account required to be subject to a control agreement under Section [__] of the Credit Agreement and Section [__] of the Security Agreement.]

6.3  Secured Party Representation.  The Secured Party represents that it has the authority to enter into this Agreement in its capacity as [administrative / collateral] agent under the Credit Agreement.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 7.  COVENANTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

7.1  Debtor Covenants.  The Debtor covenants that it shall:
(a)  not permit any Account to become subject to any control agreement or similar arrangement in favor of any person other than the Secured Party;
(b)  not close any Account or change the account number or title of any Account without the prior written consent of the Secured Party [INSERT: and prompt notice to the Bank], except that the Debtor may close an Account with a zero balance upon prior written notice to the Secured Party and the Bank if permitted under the Credit Agreement;
(c)  [INSERT: maintain each Account as a cash collateral / operating / concentration account of the type required under the Credit Agreement and not use any Account as a payroll, tax, trust, escrow or other fiduciary account unless expressly identified as such on Schedule I and permitted by the Credit Agreement];
(d)  [INSERT: take all actions reasonably requested by the Secured Party to maintain continuous perfection by control of the Secured Party’s security interest in the Accounts and Collateral]; and
(e)  [INSERT: not change its name, jurisdiction of organization or chief executive office without at least ten (10) Business Days’ prior written notice to the Secured Party and the Bank (to the extent such notice is also required under the Credit Agreement / Security Agreement).]

7.2  Bank Covenants.  The Bank covenants that it shall:
(a)  not enter into any agreement with any third party agreeing to comply with instructions of such third party as to any Account without the Secured Party’s prior written consent;
(b)  [INSERT: provide the Secured Party with not less than thirty (30) days’ prior written notice before resigning as depository bank with respect to any Account or assigning or transferring its rights and obligations hereunder (except to a successor by merger or consolidation that assumes this Agreement in writing)];
(c)  [INSERT: not amend the account documentation governing any Account in a manner that would adversely affect the Secured Party’s rights under this Agreement without the Secured Party’s prior written consent]; and
(d)  [INSERT: upon reasonable request, execute and deliver such further documents and take such further actions as the Secured Party may reasonably request to maintain, perfect or enforce the Secured Party’s control and security interest (including UCC-1 financing statement authorizations solely as to the Bank’s acknowledgment of control, if requested).]

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 8.  INDEMNIFICATION; LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

8.1  Debtor Indemnity.  The Debtor agrees to indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Bank and its officers, directors, employees, agents and affiliates (collectively, “Indemnified Persons”) from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable and documented out-of-pocket attorneys’ fees) arising out of or relating to this Agreement or the Accounts, [DELETE: except to the extent resulting from the Indemnified Person’s gross negligence or willful misconduct] [INSERT: except to the extent resulting from the Indemnified Person’s negligence, willful misconduct or bad faith, as finally determined by a court of competent jurisdiction].

8.2  [INSERT: Secured Party Non-Recourse.  The Secured Party shall have no liability to the Bank or the Debtor for any action taken or omitted in its capacity as Secured Party under this Agreement, except to the extent of its own gross negligence or willful misconduct as finally determined by a court of competent jurisdiction.  The Bank acknowledges that the Secured Party is acting solely in its agency capacity and that the Secured Party’s obligations hereunder are limited to those expressly stated.  Recourse against the Secured Party shall be limited to the extent provided in the Credit Agreement with respect to agent exculpation.]

8.3  Consequential Damages.  [DELETE: No Party shall be liable to any other Party for indirect, incidental, special, punitive or consequential damages.] [INSERT: No Party shall be liable to any other Party for indirect, incidental, special, punitive or consequential damages; provided that the foregoing shall not limit (a) the Debtor’s indemnification obligations under Section 8.1 for third-party claims or (b) any Party’s liability for its fraud or willful misconduct.]

8.4  [INSERT: Cap on Bank Liability (if insisted upon by Bank).  If the Bank requires a liability cap as a condition to execution, any such cap shall (i) be not less than $[5,000,000] per occurrence and $[10,000,000] in the aggregate, (ii) not apply to the Bank’s gross negligence, willful misconduct, bad faith, or failure to comply with a Control Notice or exclusive-control Instruction, and (iii) not limit the Bank’s obligation to turn over Collateral actually held.  **COMMENT: Prefer no cap; if commercially necessary, use floor above and carve-outs.**]

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 9.  GOVERNING LAW; JURY WAIVER; VENUE; UCC CONTROL CHOICE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

9.1  Governing Law. ================================================================================
ISSUES / RISK MEMORANDUM
Account Control Agreement — Counterparty Draft Review
================================================================================

TO:            File / Deal Team / Client
FROM:          Contracts Counsel
DATE:          [Closing Timeline — Pre-Execution]
RE:            Review of Counterparty (Depository Bank) Draft Account Control
               Agreement against Internal ACA Playbook, Executed Credit
               Agreement, Bank Standard Form, Account Details, and Related
               Correspondence / Checklists
MATTER:        Deal materials — contracts work: Review Account Control
               Agreement Counterparty Paper
DELIVERABLES:  aca-redline.docx (tracked-changes redline)
               issues-risk-memo.docx (this memorandum)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I.  EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

We reviewed the counterparty depository bank’s draft Account Control Agreement
(“ACA” or “Draft”) against: (i) the firm’s internal Account Control Agreement
Playbook (the “Playbook”); (ii) the executed Credit Agreement and related
Security / Collateral Agreement (together, the “Credit Documents”); (iii) the
depository bank’s own standard-form ACA previously circulated; (iv) the account
schedule and account-opening details for the collateral deposit accounts; and
(v) the closing checklist and related correspondence identifying ACA execution
as a condition precedent / post-closing deliverable.

Bottom line: The Draft is not acceptable as proposed. It contains multiple
high-severity deviations that impair UCC perfection-by-control, delay or
condition exclusive control, expand Bank set-off beyond market, weaken the
Bank’s standard of care, and permit unilateral Bank exit without replacement
control. Several provisions are also less favorable to the Secured Party than
the Bank’s own standard form.

We have prepared a full tracked-changes redline (aca-redline.docx) incorporating
all required modifications and insertions. This memorandum identifies every
material deviation, missing protection, and off-market term, with section
references, Playbook requirements, risk ratings, exposure analysis, and
recommended positions, and closes with a Summary Deviation Matrix.

Risk rating key:
  CRITICAL — Perfection, priority, or enforcement impairment; must-fix for CP/closing
  HIGH     — Material economic or operational risk; strong push; escalate if refused
  MEDIUM   — Market-improving; tradeable against other points
  LOW      — Clean-up, consistency, or preference

Overall negotiation posture: Require acceptance of all CRITICAL and HIGH items
as a condition to ACA reliance for Credit Document collateral requirements.
MEDIUM/LOW items may be traded if needed to close Bank negotiation promptly.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
II.  SCOPE, MATERIALS REVIEWED, AND METHODOLOGY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A.  Materials Reviewed (as identified in engagement instruction / matter file)
    1. Counterparty draft Account Control Agreement (Bank paper)
    2. Internal ACA Playbook (secured-party / agent-side requirements)
    3. Executed Credit Agreement (collateral account / control agreement covenants,
       perfection representations, CP and waterfall mechanics)
    4. Security / Collateral Agreement (grant, proceeds, deposit account definitions)
    5. Depository bank standard-form ACA
    6. Account details / Schedule of deposit accounts (numbers, titles, types)
    7. Related correspondence and closing checklists (ACA as CP or post-close item;
       authorized signers; notice contacts; fee letters)

B.  Methodology
    - Mapped each Draft section to Playbook mandatory terms and Credit Document
      collateral-account requirements.
    - Compared Draft to Bank standard form; flagged where Draft is worse than
      Bank’s own paper.
    - Tested control mechanics against UCC §§ 8-106, 9-104, 9-106, 9-304, 9-314.
    - Assessed enforcement timing (Control Notice effectiveness, implementation
      lag, default linkage).
    - Assessed insolvency / set-off / priority leakage (Excluded Claims scope).
    - Produced conforming redline and issue-by-issue positions below.

C.  Parties (placeholder names as in redline)
    Debtor:        Borrower under Credit Agreement
    Secured Party: Administrative / Collateral Agent for Secured Parties
    Bank:          Depository bank maintaining collateral Accounts

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
III.  ISSUE-BY-ISSUE ANALYSIS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

================================================================================
ISSUE 1 — Control Not Effective on Day One / Control Notice as Pseudo-Condition
           to Perfection
================================================================================
Draft Section(s):  §§ 2.3, 3.1, 3.2 (and related definitions of Control Notice)
Playbook Req.:     ACA must establish Secured Party “control” under UCC § 9-104(a)(2)
                   as of Effective Date by Bank agreement to comply with Secured
                   Party instructions without further Debtor consent. Operational
                   “springing exclusive control” via Control Notice is acceptable
                   ONLY if perfection-by-control exists continuously from signing;
                   Control Notice may not be drafted as a condition to control
                   itself.
Credit Agreement:  Requires perfected first-priority security interest in deposit
                   account collateral by control; often a CP or post-closing
                   requirement with tight cure.
Deviation:         Draft language ties Bank’s duty to comply with Secured Party
                   instructions to “after receipt of a Control Notice,” and is
                   ambiguous as to whether control exists pre-notice. This is a
                   classic bank-form ambiguity that invites argument that control
                   (and thus perfection under § 9-314) springs only upon notice.
Risk Rating:       CRITICAL
Exposure Analysis: If a bankruptcy intervenes before Control Notice, trustee or
                   competing creditor may argue Secured Party lacked control and
                   thus lacked perfected security interest in deposit accounts /
                   cash, converting intended perfected deposit-account collateral
                   into potentially unperfected or proceeds-only claims. Loss of
                   perfection on cash collateral is often total economic loss of
                   that collateral pool. Also jeopardizes any CP certificate that
                   “all collateral accounts are subject to control agreements
                   perfecting by control.”
Recommended Position: MUST INSERT express acknowledgment that Secured Party has
                   control under § 9-104(a)(2) from Effective Date; Control Notice
                   only switches operational regime from Debtor-direction-permitted
                   to exclusive Secured Party direction. See redline §§ 2.3, 3.1(c),
                   3.2.
Fallback:          None on substance. Cosmetic re-ordering acceptable if operative
                   control sentence is retained.

================================================================================
ISSUE 2 — Control Notice Conditioned on Event of Default
================================================================================
Draft Section(s):  § 3.2(a); Exhibit A certification
Playbook Req.:     Secured Party may deliver Control Notice at any time in sole
                   discretion; no EOD predicate; no certification of default.
Credit Agreement:  Agent must be able to lock accounts promptly upon default,
                   anticipated default, or as otherwise permitted (e.g., cash
                   dominion triggers, reserve mechanics); waiting for formal EOD
                   and cure periods can destroy value.
Deviation:         Draft permits Control Notice only “following the occurrence of
                   an Event of Default” and Exhibit A requires Secured Party to
                   certify EOD is continuing.
Risk Rating:       CRITICAL
Exposure Analysis: Conditions exclusive control on disputed default status.
                   Debtor may seek TRO arguing no EOD, freezing enforcement.
                   Bank may refuse to implement pending “confirmation” of default.
                   Inconsistent with springing cash dominion and protective
                   advance mechanics. Creates litigation risk at precisely the
                   moment speed is required.
Recommended Position: DELETE EOD condition and Exhibit A default certification.
                   Control Notice at sole discretion, anytime. See redline
                   § 3.2(a), § 3.2(c), Exhibit A.
Fallback:          If Bank demands comfort, allow optional (not required)
                   reference to Secured Party’s rights under Credit Documents,
                   still without Bank inquiry or Debtor challenge right.

================================================================================
ISSUE 3 — Implementation Lag for Control Notice (Multi-Business-Day)
================================================================================
Draft Section(s):  § 3.4 (Bank “reasonable period” up to three Business Days)
Playbook Req.:     Control Notice effective on receipt; implement same day if
                   received before noon local time, otherwise next Business Day;
                   other instructions within one Business Day / applicable cut-off.
Credit Agreement:  Enforcement and cash dominion assume prompt lockbox/account
                   freeze.
Deviation:         Up to three Business Days to implement exclusive control.
Risk Rating:       CRITICAL
Exposure Analysis: Debtor can drain Accounts during lag. Same-day wire-out risk
                   is the core operational failure mode of ACAs. Three days is
                   off-market and unacceptable for agency financings.
Recommended Position: Replace with same-day / next-day standard in redline § 3.4;
                   require written confirmation of implementation within one
                   Business Day (§ 3.2(b)(iv)).
Fallback:          Next Business Day hard outside; no “reasonable period” softener.

================================================================================
ISSUE 4 — Open-Ended Bank Set-Off (“Any Other Obligations”)
================================================================================
Draft Section(s):  §§ 2.2, 5.2(c)
Playbook Req.:     Bank subordination of liens/set-off to Secured Party, subject
                   only to narrow Excluded Claims: (i) customary account fees,
                   (ii) returned items/chargebacks on the Accounts, (iii) overdrafts
                   on the same Account — each account-specific and time-limited.
                   No cross-affiliate or unrelated facility set-off.
Credit Agreement:  First-priority perfected liens; intercreditor/priority leakage
                   via bank set-off undermines secured claim and borrowing base
                   cash treatment.
Deviation:         Draft allows set-off for “any other obligations of the Debtor
                   to the Bank, whether or not related to the Accounts,” and weak
                   pre-control set-off wording.
Risk Rating:       CRITICAL
Exposure Analysis: Bank can wipe collateral cash for unrelated loans, derivatives,
                   cards, or affiliate exposure. In distress, Bank becomes de facto
                   senior creditor on cash without intercreditor agreement. Can
                   destroy recovery model and trigger borrowing-base / liquidity
                   defaults.
Recommended Position: DELETE open-ended clause; limit Excluded Claims as in
                   redline § 5.2; strengthen § 2.2 waiver; add Excluded Claims Cap
                   post-Control Notice (§ 5.2A); time-limit returned-item lookback
                   (e.g., 180 days) and fee aging.
Fallback:          Modest returned-item lookback extension; small dollar cap
                   carve-out for fees only. No unrelated obligations.

================================================================================
ISSUE 5 — “To the Bank’s Knowledge” Qualification on No Prior Control Agreements
================================================================================
Draft Section(s):  § 2.1(d)
Playbook Req.:     Flat Bank representation: no other active control agreement or
                   third-party instruction arrangement on the Accounts.
Credit Agreement:  Exclusive control / priority assumptions.
Deviation:         Knowledge qualifier on absence of competing control arrangements.
Risk Rating:       HIGH
Exposure Analysis: Knowledge qualifier shifts risk of undisclosed prior ACA or
                   “triple party” arrangement to Secured Party; undermines
                   exclusive control narrative and diligence reliance.
Recommended Position: Delete knowledge qualifier; flat rep + ongoing covenant
                   not to enter other control agreements (§§ 2.1, 2.4, 6.1(e), 7.2(a)).
Fallback:          “To the actual knowledge of the Bank officers responsible for
                   the Accounts, after reasonable inquiry of deposit operations”
                   — only if Bank refuses flat rep, and pair with strong covenant.

================================================================================
ISSUE 6 — Standard of Care: Gross Negligence / Willful Misconduct Only
================================================================================
Draft Section(s):  §§ 4.1, 8.1
Playbook Req.:     Bank liable for ordinary negligence, willful misconduct, and bad
                   faith; indemnity carve-out matches. “Same care as similar
                   accounts” industry standard is acceptable framing.
Bank Standard Form: Often ordinary negligence for operational errors.
Deviation:         Draft limits Bank liability and expands Debtor indemnity carve-
                   out only for gross negligence or willful misconduct.
Risk Rating:       HIGH
Exposure Analysis: Failed wires, misapplied Control Notices, or negligent release
                   of funds may escape Bank liability under “gross negligence”
                   threshold. Secured Party/Debtor bears loss from ordinary
                   operational failures — precisely the risk ACA is meant to
                   allocate to the Bank’s control of the plumbing.
Recommended Position: Ordinary negligence standard as in redline §§ 4.1 and 8.1.
Fallback:          Ordinary negligence for Control Notice / exclusive-instruction
                   failures; gross negligence for other duties — split standard.

================================================================================
ISSUE 7 — Bank Unilateral Termination (30 Days, No Replacement Control)
================================================================================
Draft Section(s):  § 10.3
Playbook Req.:     Bank termination only on extended notice (60 days), with
                   mandatory cooperation to transition and effectiveness deferred
                   until replacement control arrangement satisfactory to Secured
                   Party is in place (unless zero-balance close with consent).
Credit Agreement:  Continuous perfection covenants; loss of ACA without replacement
                   is immediate defaults / mandatory prepayment risk.
Deviation:         Bank may terminate on 30 days’ notice with no replacement-
                   control condition.
Risk Rating:       HIGH
Exposure Analysis: Bank can force unperfected gap. In stress, strategic termination
                   pressure. Agent may be unable to replace bank and re-control
                   accounts inside 30 days (KYC, new ACA negotiation).
Recommended Position: 60 days + replacement control condition + transition
                   cooperation as in redline § 10.3; resignation notice covenant
                   § 7.2(b).
Fallback:          45 days with replacement-control condition hard requirement.

================================================================================
ISSUE 8 — Account Statements and Information Access “Upon Request” Only
================================================================================
Draft Section(s):  § 5.3
Playbook Req.:     Automatic concurrent statements to Secured Party; view-only
                   online access if available; balance confirmations on request;
                   Debtor authorization hardwired.
Credit Agreement:  Cash dominion, reporting, and reserve calculations require
                   timely account visibility.
Deviation:         Statements only upon request; no online access or automatic
                   feed; no express Debtor direction to Bank.
Risk Rating:       HIGH
Exposure Analysis: Blind as to balances and drains; delays detection of leakage;
                   weakens monitoring covenants and field exam efficiency.
Recommended Position: Automatic concurrent delivery + online view-only + on-
                   request confirmations + Debtor authorization (§ 5.3 redline).
Fallback:          Monthly automatic statements + 1-Business-Day response to
                   balance inquiries if online access truly unavailable.

================================================================================
ISSUE 9 — Missing UCC § 9-304 Bank’s Jurisdiction Designation (New York)
================================================================================
Draft Section(s):  § 9 (Governing Law) — gap
Playbook Req.:     Express designation of Bank’s jurisdiction as New York for
                   UCC § 9-304 purposes; amendment of account docs to the extent
                   inconsistent; note on Bank’s books.
Credit Agreement:  NY law financing package; predictability of perfection rules.
Deviation:         Draft has generic NY governing law but no § 9-304 jurisdiction
                   designation; account documentation may point to Bank’s home
                   state.
Risk Rating:       HIGH
Exposure Analysis: Perfection and priority rules for deposit accounts follow
                   bank’s jurisdiction (§ 9-304). Silent or conflicting designation
                   creates multi-state perfection risk and opinion issues.
Recommended Position: Insert § 9.2 as in redline; align account docs.
Fallback:          Accept Bank home-state jurisdiction ONLY if Security Agreement
                   and opinions are conformed and Playbook choice-of-law matrix
                   cleared — escalate to opinion committee.

================================================================================
ISSUE 10 — Missing / Weak Additional Accounts Mechanic
================================================================================
Draft Section(s):  Gap (no clear joinder/supplement process)
Playbook Req.:     Automatic or short-fuse (5 Business Day) supplement to Schedule I
                   / joinder for any new Bank account required to be controlled
                   under Credit Documents.
Credit Agreement:  Future collateral accounts must be promptly controlled.
Deviation:         Draft is static to listed accounts; no covenanted process.
Risk Rating:       HIGH
Exposure Analysis: New accounts opened in ordinary course may sit uncontrolled,
                   creating perfection gaps and CP/post-close checklist failures.
Recommended Position: Insert § 2.5 and Schedule I update language; Debtor covenant
                   § 7.1.
Fallback:          10 Business Days if Bank ops require, with interim “blocked
                   pending joinder” instruction.

================================================================================
ISSUE 11 — Missing Prohibition on Other Control Agreements
================================================================================
Draft Section(s):  Gap / weak implication only
Playbook Req.:     Express Bank covenant not to enter other ACAs on the Accounts
                   without Secured Party consent; Debtor mirror covenant.
Deviation:         No clear affirmative prohibition going forward.
Risk Rating:       HIGH
Exposure Analysis: Dual-control or junior-control arrangements can create
                   conflicting entitlement orders and priority disputes.
Recommended Position: Insert §§ 2.4, 7.1(a), 7.2(a).
Fallback:          None material.

================================================================================
ISSUE 12 — Amendments Require All Parties; Agent Cannot Update Authorized
           Persons List Unilaterally
================================================================================
Draft Section(s):  § 12.1; notices schedule
Playbook Req.:     Secured Party may update its notice details and authorized
                   persons for Instructions by notice to Bank without Debtor
                   consent; Debtor consent needed only for amendments increasing
                   Debtor burdens.
Credit Agreement:  Agent personnel change frequently; cannot depend on Debtor
                   countersignature in default scenario.
Deviation:         All-party amendment formulation; static signer schedule.
Risk Rating:       HIGH
Exposure Analysis: Stale authorized-signer list → Bank rejects Control Notice in
                   a default — catastrophic operational failure.
Recommended Position: Redline § 12.1 and Schedule II update rights; email
                   Instructions from designated addresses (§ 3.3).
Fallback:          Bank may require callback verification on changes, but not
                   Debtor consent.

================================================================================
ISSUE 13 — Debtor Fee Debit Rights Unrestricted Even After Control Notice
================================================================================
Draft Section(s):  § 5.1
Playbook Req.:     Fee debits only as Excluded Claims; after Control Notice, no
                   debit without Secured Party consent or court order (Debtor
                   remains liable).
Deviation:         Bank may debit fees “at any time.”
Risk Rating:       MEDIUM
Exposure Analysis: Post-default fee sweeps reduce controlled cash; usually small
                   dollars but bad precedent and can interact with Excluded Claims
